summary:
CropCast is a spatial crop recommendation tool. A user picks a location on a map, and the system retrieves local climate data from NASA POWER (temperature, humidity, rainfall) and soil pH from SoilGrids. A custom Multi-Layer Perceptron with a softmax output then ranks 22 crops by suitability and returns the top five. On held-out data, the model reaches 92.5% accuracy, and the correct crop appears in its top five every time. The model runs behind a FastAPI service that connects to our Express backend, and it flags when soil data is unavailable and a default pH was used.

NASA’s Earth observation data is the foundation of the system. It turns satellite-derived climate records into practical planting guidance for any point on Earth, including places with no local agronomic advice. Smallholder farmers, who are most exposed to climate variability, can make better decisions about what to grow, which supports food security and more resilient farming.
details:
CropCast lets a user pick any point on a map and get a ranked list of the five crops best suited to it. The backend retrieves 25-year climatology (Jan 2001 to Dec 2025) from NASA POWER (temperature, relative humidity, precipitation) and topsoil pH from ISRIC SoilGrids. These four features are standardized and passed to a Multi-Layer Perceptron (64→32 ReLU layers, dropout, softmax over 22 crops) built in TensorFlow/Keras. The softmax output is ranked into a top-5 “suitability score” list. The model reaches 92.5% accuracy on a held-out test set, and the correct crop is always in the top 5.

The model is served by a FastAPI service (POST /predict) with input validation, clear error codes, and a flag showing when soil data was unavailable and a default pH was used. [Add only if finished: An Express backend proxies requests from the map frontend.]

Tools: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, TensorFlow/Keras, FastAPI, requests-cache, [Node/Express, Leaflet].

Limitations we considered: the model is trained on the public Kaggle Crop Recommendation dataset, which lacks coordinates and real field validation. We dropped N, P and K because no global source supplies them at runtime. Our annual-average climate features differ from the growing-season conditions the dataset describes.

Intended impact: free, location-aware planting guidance for farmers and planners where local agronomic advice is scarce.
